bullets.title: META: Iris AI chip, compute doubling, AI monetization, and bullish fintwit sentiment
bullets.body: Meta's in-house 'Iris' AI chip enters production in September as part of its 4-gen MTIA program, with plans to deploy 7GW compute this year and double to 14GW by 2027. Meta has also begun charging businesses to use its AI models for the first time. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged META approaching its first close above the 200-day MA since April, Ark Invest bought 34,080 shares, and traders are broadly bullish — one calling META 'better positioned than consensus thinks' and another suggesting $1,200 as a target. A separate valuation argument notes META's 7GW compute + competitive models trade at negative implied value vs. xAI's $1T+ valuation on only 1GW.

bullets.title: NVDA: Morgan Stanley NDR flags multi-year memory shortage; compute costs exceed salaries
bullets.body: Per Morgan Stanley's NVIDIA non-deal roadshow takeaways, NVIDIA expects the memory shortage to persist for several years and has the best visibility into global AI demand. Separately, NVIDIA VP of applied deep learning Bryan Catanzaro stated that compute costs for his team now exceed employee salary costs, underlining the scale of AI infrastructure spend.

bullets.title: MU: $250B US investment pledge, NY fab groundbreaking, and 2026 earnings inflection
bullets.body: Micron shares rose 7% after announcing expanded U.S. chipmaking investment, with the company now targeting $250B in domestic investment through 2035. Micron officially poured concrete for its first New York fab in Clay, NY. One fintwit account noted MU will likely earn more in 2026 than the prior 35 years combined, and a separate analyst thread examined how much bad news is priced in via scenario modeling.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand broadening beyond hyperscalers — bullish for NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE
bullets.body: A detailed thread flags AI infrastructure capex broadening to neocloud providers, European data centers, sovereign compute, and enterprise coding — with frontier labs no longer the dominant demand driver. Memory prices are already up ~4x in this cycle and could rise another 2-3x, though 85%+ gross margins are unsustainable long-term. CPU demand is also surging due to large-scale OpenAI/Anthropic partnerships with Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.

bullets.title: LITE: InP becomes critical AI bottleneck; Lumentum presenting at LightCounting July 15
bullets.body: Lumentum has flagged InP (Indium Phosphide) capacity expansion on recent earnings calls, with one fintwit account noting InP is transitioning from an optics subtopic to a physical AI infrastructure bottleneck. Lumentum exec Oleg Shchekin will present on VCSEL-based wide-parallel optical interconnects for AI scale-up networks at LightCounting virtual conference on July 15. A separate bear case flags potential photonics cyclical oversupply as a risk for LITE, COHR, and AAOI.

bullets.title: Taiwan semiconductor exports surge 43.9% in H1 2026; DRAM up 158.5%
bullets.body: Taiwan semiconductor exports in June rose 33.4% YoY to $24.11B; Q2 2026 totaled $71.15B (+43.7% YoY) and H1 2026 hit $133.17B (+43.9%). DRAM exports surged 158.5% to $18.55B in H1 2026, reflecting the ongoing AI-driven memory demand cycle.

bullets.title: Server DRAM prices keep rising on tight supply; 4x cycle gain with more to come
bullets.body: TrendForce notes server DRAM prices continuing upward despite long-term agreement caps limiting maximum increases. A fintwit thread argues memory prices have risen ~4x in the current cycle and could climb another 2-3x, but gross margins above 85% are ultimately unsustainable, setting up a future price reversal when that threshold is approached.

bullets.title: META: Rumor of internally developed Mythos 5-level model; deployment expected in months
bullets.body: A fintwit account citing ICML ground-level conversations reports a rumor that Meta has internally developed a model at the 'Mythos 5' capability level, with deployment expected within the next few months. Separately, Tencent is reportedly leading a deal to unwind Meta's $2B Manus acquisition.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury auction yields 5.058%, highest since pre-GFC
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury bond auction drew a yield of 5.058%, the highest level since the run-up to the Global Financial Crisis. Meanwhile, a separate post noted the Hindenburg Omen has been triggered 11 times on Nasdaq over the past month, the most in history, though the indicator's predictive value is debated.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike odds reach ~67% for September FOMC
bullets.body: One fintwit account flagged markets pricing a nearly 2/3 probability of a rate hike at the September FOMC meeting, a sharp shift in monetary policy expectations. Separately, Polymarket was cited pricing 57% probability of no rate change in September — the two data points bracket an unusually wide range of market uncertainty.

bullets.title: Japan PPI surges 7.1% YoY in June, fastest since early 2023; yen strengthens on GPIF pivot
bullets.body: Japan's June producer price index rose 7.1% YoY, beating the 6.8% BOJ forecast and accelerating from 6.3% prior, supporting the case for BOJ rate hikes. Finance Minister Katayama signaled measures to encourage GPIF and households to increase domestic Japanese asset investment, triggering USD/JPY to fall ~0.6% and Japan's 10Y yield to ease ~7-10bps.

bullets.title: TSLA: Fintwit skeptics cite trading volume drop, -10% YTD vs Nasdaq +16%
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts are bearish on Tesla, with one noting TSLA is down 10% YTD while Nasdaq is up 16%, and citing TSLA trading volume dropping to pre-Trump lows as evidence of community deterioration. Another account exited TSLA in December and avoided buyback, characterizing the situation as better opportunities elsewhere. Bullish offset: a retweet called FSD 'magical' and Gavin Baker credited Tesla with doing more to decarbonize the world than all environmental activists combined.

bullets.title: BE: Bloom Energy faces strategic scandium supply risk; equity risk is nonlinear
bullets.body: A detailed multi-part thread on Bloom Energy identifies scandium sourcing as a genuine strategic constraint, though available evidence does not confirm an imminent 2026 production stoppage. Scandium currently represents less than 1% of system revenue; the primary equity risk is markets capitalizing a 3-5 GW volume trajectory that cannot be physically supplied. Risk is described as nonlinear and conditional on undisclosed factors.

bullets.title: NFLX: Netflix considering always-on linear channels
bullets.body: Netflix is reportedly exploring the addition of always-on linear channels, representing a potential shift from its pure on-demand model toward linear viewing experiences. No financial details were disclosed.

bullets.title: MSFT: Xbox cuts 1,600 jobs; carbon emissions up 25% YoY
bullets.body: Microsoft's Xbox division is cutting 1,600 jobs amid broader corporate restructuring. Separately, Microsoft's carbon emissions rose 25% last year, contradicting the company's sustainability and net-zero commitments — a potential ESG-related headwind.

bullets.title: Grok 4.5 claims #1 on multiple AI benchmarks; GPT-5.6 Sol sets ARC-AGI-3 SOTA
bullets.body: Grok 4.5 is reported as ranking #1 on AutomationBench-AA (51%) and Terminal-Bench v2, ahead of Claude Fable 5 (49%). Separately, GPT-5.6 Sol set a new SOTA on ARC-AGI-3 at 7.8%, described as the first verified frontier model to beat an ARC-AGI-3 game. Fintwit debate continues on AI lab vs. startup competitive dynamics, with recent data favoring labs.

bullets.title: Anthropic ARR hits $69B; FCF positive in Q2 with accelerating daily growth
bullets.body: Yipit estimates Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate has reached $69B, with month-over-month growth accelerating from ~$400M to ~$550M average daily ARR increase. A separate podcast takeaway confirmed Anthropic turned free-cash-flow positive and profitable in Q2, with April and May both FCF positive.

bullets.title: Data center pipeline extends to 12-year backlog; 338GW in queue
bullets.body: One fintwit account flags that the data center project pipeline, at 338GW, would now take 12 years to clear at current build rates (up from 10 years prior), raising questions about potential GPU and memory infrastructure over-commitment. Counter-narrative: AI capex is broadening to new demand vectors including sovereign compute and enterprise coding.

bullets.title: Typhoon Bavi approaches Taiwan — potentially largest in 40 years
bullets.body: Typhoon Bavi is approaching Taiwan and may be the largest typhoon to hit the island in 40 years; Taipei and other cities/counties have already cancelled work and school. Taiwan is a critical node in global semiconductor supply chains, particularly for TSMC.

bullets.title: Carry trade conditions at most favorable since dot-com era; USD at 3-week low
bullets.body: Fintwit flags foreign currency carry trades at their most favorable conditions since the dot-com bubble burst, raising sustainability questions. Simultaneously, the US Dollar Index fell to a three-week low amid signs of US-Iran de-escalation. S&P 500 is holding at the 50-day moving average heading into earnings season.
